sentences.text: A connected agent is a specialist.
It is like a receptionist who transfers a payroll question to Human Resources.
There are two ways to do this.
In both cases the specialist answers with its own sources, and the main agent gets the result back so it can continue the conversation.
There are two ways.
One: the orchestrator decides by itself, based on the description.
Two: a topic redirects the conversation to the agent, and its inputs and outputs become topic variables.
Choose the orchestrator option when you want flexibility, and the Redirect when you want to control exactly when work is handed over.
In the main agent's instructions, you can reference another agent by typing a forward slash and choosing its name.
This tells the main agent when to use that specialist.
It is a simple way to guide the orchestrator without writing complicated rules.
Some limits show up on the exam.
A main agent with connected agents cannot also be used as a connected agent.
Child agents respect the Use general knowledge setting of the main agent.
And citations can be lost on the way back.
Memorize these three points very well.
Everything depends on the descriptions.
If each agent has a clear and distinct description, the orchestrator hands work over well.
If they look alike, it hesitates.
Write what each specialist can do and what it cannot, with simple words, and do not repeat the same phrases across agents.
